title: A4 Continuous Experimentation - UI Engagement Test
description: Experiment: Does the new UI (v2 canary) increase user engagement compared to stable (v1)? Hypothesis: Users who see the prettier v2 UI will send more requests per session than v1 users.

options.content:
## 🧪 Experiment: UI Engagement Test

**Hypothesis:** The new UI (Canary v2) is more engaging and causes users to interact more frequently.

**Setup:**
- **Traffic Split:** 90% users see Stable (v1), 10% see Canary (v2)
- **Expected Behavior:** Even though v2 has fewer users (10%), those users should generate MORE total requests if the UI is more engaging

**Decision Criteria:**
- ✅ **Accept v2** if: Request rate for v2 > Request rate for v1 (despite having 90% fewer users)
- ❌ **Reject v2** if: Request rate similar or lower (UI doesn't increase engagement)

**Interpretation:**
- If v2 RPS > v1 RPS → v2 users are ~9x more engaged per user → **Hypothesis confirmed**
- If v2 RPS ≈ v1 RPS → Engagement similar → **Hypothesis rejected**
- If v2 RPS < v1 RPS → v2 actually reduces engagement → **Hypothesis strongly rejected**

panels.title: Request Rate per Version (KEY METRIC)
panels.description: Canary (v2) should show HIGHER RPS than Stable (v1) if users are more engaged. Remember: v2 only has 10% of users, so higher RPS means much higher per-user engagement.

panels.title: Engagement Multiplier
panels.description: How many times more engaged are v2 users compared to v1 users? Calculated as: (v2 RPS / 0.1) / (v1 RPS / 0.9). Values > 1 mean v2 users are more engaged.

panels.title: Decision Recommendation
panels.description: Automated recommendation based on engagement multiplier. > 1.5 = Strong Accept, 1.0-1.5 = Accept, 0.8-1.0 = Neutral, < 0.8 = Reject

panels.title: Ham vs Spam Classification Rate
panels.description: Classification results by version. Verify both versions classify messages similarly (no regression in model behavior).

panels.title: Total Requests per Version (Cumulative)
panels.description: Absolute cumulative request counts. Shows total volume over time. v2 should overtake v1 if engagement hypothesis is correct.

panels.title: P95 Latency per Version (Safety Metric)
panels.description: Verify new UI doesn't degrade performance. Both versions should have similar latency.
